claims.hypothesis: How many protostellar cores does G328.24-0.55 host and which dominates?
claims.experiment: Gaussian fits to the ALMA 1.3 mm continuum image
claims.result: Five cores (MM1a, MM1b, MM1c, MM2, MM3); MM1a has the largest peak and integrated flux
claims.finding: The region is fragmented and MM1a dominates

evidence.quote: The dust continuum image reveals 5 protostellar objects (MM1a, MM1b, MM1c, MM2 and MM3), with MM1a dominating the region.

claims.hypothesis: Do the cores differ in excitation conditions and evolutionary state?
claims.experiment: Count detected lines per core and fit CH3OH rotation diagrams
claims.result: 70, 49, 26, 7 and 8 transitions; T_ex ~183, 168, 110 K for MM1a-c
claims.finding: Variation in line counts reflects different excitation conditions; MM1a-c are hot cores

evidence.quote: This variation in the number of detected molecular transitions supports different excitation conditions in these objects.

claims.hypothesis: Does CH3OH trace a rotating structure around MM1a?
claims.result: East-west velocity gradient with FWHM peaking at the continuum peak
claims.finding: A rotating structure, probably an envelope, around MM1a

evidence.quote: The velocity gradient of CH$_{3}$OH emission is also found to trace a rotating structure, probably an envelope of gas around MM1a.

claims.hypothesis: Is there a bipolar outflow from MM1a?
claims.experiment: Integrated blue- and red-shifted CO 2-1 emission overlaid on the continuum; dynamical timescale
claims.result: Bipolar lobes of 31080 and 14840 au; average t_d 1.03e4 yr
claims.finding: MM1a is likely the driving source of a bipolar outflow

evidence.quote: Bipolar outflow traced by CO emission is seen towards MM1a.

claims.hypothesis: What is the nature of MM1a?
claims.experiment: Combined mass, temperature, line richness, rotation and outflow
claims.result: 23.2 Msun, T_ex ~183 K, richest chemistry, outflow and rotation
claims.finding: MM1a is a massive protostellar object still accreting and driving outflow

evidence.quote: The properties of MM1a clearly point to the existence of a massive protostellar object that is still undergoing accretion and outflow in its early formative stage.

evidence.quote: High resolution and sensitivity ALMA continuum and spectral lines observations provide a great opportunity to uncover the fine structure of G328.24

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Spectral diversity could also arise from observational biases, grain-mantle composition differences or excitation; sensitivity bias was ruled out and excitation favoured

evidence.quote: The diversity in millimeter spectra from the several cores could also be the result of other factors, including observational biases

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Positional offsets between ATCA, Spitzer and ALMA peaks attributed to absolute astrometric accuracy rather than physical offsets

evidence.quote: appears to be an instrumental effect, likely due to differences in the absolute coordinate accuracy of these observations

limitations_admitted.value: No excitation temperature for MM2 and MM3 (too few CH3OH lines), so their masses and column densities depend on an assumed 20 K

evidence.quote: determining the specific temperatures of MM2 and MM3 will be of great importance in estimating their precise masses and column densities

limitations_admitted.value: MM1b may host an undetected disk; its evolutionary status is uncertain

evidence.quote: it may still host a disk that remains undetected due to weak emission or an unfavorable orientation

referee_caveats_inferred: CH3OH T_ex (gas, hot-core, LTE) is used as dust temperature for mass; no uncertainty propagation into masses and T_d error treatment is inconsistent
A single optically thin dust opacity of 0.19 cm^2/g and gas-to-dust 100 with no discussion of free-free or line contamination in the 1.3 mm continuum or of optical depth in the dense cores
Rotation claim rests on one moment-1 map of a line with FWHM ~6 km/s at about beam-size scales; no PV diagram, Keplerian fit or comparison with outflow contamination
Line-ID table lists typos (HNCO at 19.737 GHz) and identical linewidths repeated across many lines (7.42 km/s), suggesting fit limits rather than measurements
Statement that MM1a is the outflow driver is inferred, not established; MM1b/c as drivers not tested
